brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: A portable electronics organizer: a base
requirements.evidence: Three hex bases: piece:0,0,0 (full), piece:-1,0,0 (half-w), piece:-1,1,0 (full), joined into one body.
bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3-compartment full-depth bin) and bin:-1,0,0~hex-bin-half-w-full-div2 (2-compartment bin). Both drop into their cells and lift out.

notch:0#0,1#notch2 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf, a notch drawer frame) fills the empty spot between the bases at (0,0) and (-1,1). It was accepted as a drawer, but no separate drawer tray was listed in the build, so I did not confirm a pull-out tray is present.
handle:-1,1,0;top sits on the cover cover:-1,1,0;full;top, with its inserts.
The build is a compact, single-body assembly (about 364 x 105 x 413 mm) with a handle. The configurator does not check weight, strength or material, so portability in the real sense is not verified.

finish.summary: Built a compact organizer: three joined hex bases with two removable bins, a notch-mounted drawer frame between them, and a carry handle on the top cover of the (-1,1) base. Open faces are capped and joints bolted. check_build is clean on rule errors with meshClash clear; one LOOSE_BODY warning remains on the half-w base, which no joint-bolt socket was offered to fix. No props were added, since the brief is about the hardware.

lines.label: Bin, west half, full depth, 2 compartments
M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
